cases.question: Who introduced retrieval-augmented generation?
cases.answer_text: The credited authors are Patrick Lewis, Ethan Perez, Aleksandra Piktus, Fabio Petroni, Vladimir Karpukhin, Naman Goyal, Heinrich Küttler, Mike Lewis, Wen‑tau Yih, Tim Rocktäschel, Sebastian Riedel, and Douwe Kiela [S1]. Retrieval‑augmented generation (RAG) is defined as a fine‑tuning approach that endows pre‑trained, parametric‑memory generation models with a non‑parametric memory, combining a pre‑trained seq2seq transformer with a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed by a neural retriever [S2].

cases.question: Compare RAG-Token and RAG-Sequence.
cases.answer_text: RAG-Token draws a separate latent document for each target token, retrieving the top‑K documents and having the generator produce a distribution for the next token conditioned on each document before marginalizing across them for each token generation step. RAG-Sequence treats the retrieved document as a single latent variable, retrieving the top‑K documents and having the generator produce the full output‑sequence probability for each document, then marginalizing across the documents. Sources: [S1] [S2]
